change.title: ao-replay/9036-r1
change.description:
feat(telemetry): break slow launches and frozen frames into named steps
fix(e2e): stub launchSteps in the fake desktop bridge
change.author: ronish

findings.title: Docs say only `first` or `cold` launches carry main's steps; `update` launches carry them too
findings.body: `launchProperties` attaches the steps whenever `start.kind === "cold"` (frontend/src/renderer/lib/launch-telemetry.ts:135). `readLaunchKind` returns `update` for a cold start on a new `app_version`, so `update` launches send `to_app_ready_ms`, `to_window_shown_ms`, `to_server_spawn_ms`, `to_server_ready_ms` and `server_reused` as well. The table row here (line 914) and the bullet at line 928 both say "on a `first` or `cold` launch". Anyone building a dashboard from the doc would expect `update` launches to have no steps. Say "first, cold or update" in both places.

findings.title: The steps IPC is awaited after the pagehide listener is removed, so it has no bound and no close fallback
findings.body: The race ends and the `pagehide` listener is removed at lines 131-132. Only then does line 135 await `readLaunchSteps()`, which is an IPC round trip with no timeout. If the window closes during that await, nothing sends the event. The `sendOnClose` path exists to prevent exactly that loss, and the doc comment at line 93 still says the function "Resolves within USABLE_WAIT_MS". The main handler is synchronous (frontend/src/main.ts:3734), so the window is small. A busy main process widens it. Either read the steps before the race, or keep the listener until the IPC has resolved and pass the steps into `properties()` on close too.

contracts.action: New IPC handler telemetry:launchSteps returns main's launch marks to the renderer
contracts.equivalent_path: telemetry:takeLaunchStart and telemetry:takeResourceSummary handlers next to it
contracts.before_after: The sibling handlers check `trustedShellWebContents.get(event.sender.id) !== event.sender` and return null. The new handler does the same check. Unlike takeLaunchStart it does not delete anything, so repeated reads are harmless. The renderer reads it once, after the usable race, only for cold launches.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change. The extra step properties go out on ao.launches.timed.
contracts.failure_mode: An untrusted sender gets null. A renderer-side rejection is caught in readLaunchSteps and the event is sent without steps. The one gap is a window closing during the await (see the finding on launch-telemetry.ts:135).

contracts.action: The first-run flag is read with existsSync on <dataDir>/ao.db at module load
contracts.equivalent_path: Daemon store open, which creates ao.db (backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go store open step)
contracts.before_after: The check runs synchronously at top level, before initializeDesktopLog and before any daemon spawn, so the daemon cannot have created the DB yet. A daemon the user started earlier with `ao start` has already created it, so that launch correctly reads as not first. Only the first cold window gets firstRun (main.ts:1158-1160), and a reload gets no launch start at all.
contracts.visible_effect: launch_kind is `first` instead of `cold` on a fresh data directory. `first` takes precedence over `update` (launch-telemetry.ts:56).
contracts.failure_mode: existsSync cannot throw. A launch that dies before the daemon creates ao.db still reads as first on the next run, which is acceptable.

contracts.action: Daemon emits ao.daemon.ready and ao.daemon.startup_reconciled through the telemetry sink
contracts.equivalent_path: ao.daemon.started emission at daemon.go:350 and the remotePayloadAllowlist / sanitizeRemotePayload export path
contracts.before_after: Both new events have allowlist entries covering every step key. A test asserts the daemon's step list matches the allowlist keys. sanitizeRemotePayload passes int64 values through. The background event is only emitted when ctx.Err() == nil.
contracts.visible_effect: None in the product. Two extra telemetry events per start.
contracts.failure_mode: A step that was never reached is absent from the payload. Early returns emit nothing. The restore goroutine uses its own startupSteps and the ready callback runs once, so there is no shared-state race.

contracts.action: Bound on the ao.launches.timed wait after the new IPC read
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing Promise.race of usable against USABLE_WAIT_MS and pagehide
contracts.before_after: The race is bounded by USABLE_WAIT_MS (60 s). The new readLaunchSteps await sits after the race and outside both the timer and the pagehide handler, with no limit of its own.
contracts.visible_effect: The telemetry event can be delayed, or lost if the window closes during the await. Nothing user-visible.
contracts.failure_mode: If main never answers, launchProperties never resolves and no launch event is sent. The handler is synchronous, so this is unlikely.

summary: The change is sound overall. I read all 20 files and traced the long-frame phase arithmetic against the new tests by hand; the expected values come out right. Telemetry privacy handling holds: `invokerName` and `bundleName` reject URLs and ids, and the backend allowlist covers every daemon step key. Two small items, neither a blocker. The docs say only `first` or `cold` launches carry main's steps, but `update` launches carry them too. The new IPC read in `launchProperties` happens after the pagehide fallback is removed and has no bound of its own, so a window closing during it loses the event.
